findings.title: Non-atomic partition lock creation breaks mutual exclusion
findings.body: OffsetTracker._get_partition_lock does get then setdefault on partition_locks without holding a global lock. Two threads submitting/completing/committing the same Partition concurrently can each create a different threading.Lock and then guard add_offset/complete_offset/get_committable_offsets/mark_committed with different locks. Mutual exclusion is then lost, causing lost offset updates, wrong committable calculation, duplicate processing or skipping offsets. Use a single global lock to protect lock creation and dict access.

findings.title: Unbounded work queues allow unbounded memory growth
findings.body: FixedQueuePool creates queue.Queue() with no maxsize and submit() never blocks, while poll() only emits metrics. If workers are slow the consumer keeps pulling from Kafka and enqueuing WorkItem objects holding full Messages, growing memory without bound until OOM, contrary to the docstring claim of natural backpressure. Use bounded queues with blocking submit or explicit backpressure.

findings.title: Closing one strategy shuts down factory-shared queue pool
findings.body: FixedQueuePool is created once in ResultsStrategyFactory.__init__ and shared by every strategy returned from create_with_partitions, but SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close() and join() call queue_pool.shutdown() which stops all workers and shuts down all queues. After a Kafka rebalance Arroyo closes the old strategy and creates a new one reusing the same dead pool, so subsequent processing stalls or raises and the consumer never recovers without restart. Pool lifetime must be owned by the factory, strategy close should not destroy it.

findings.title: Each strategy leaks a commit thread sharing one tracker with stale commits
findings.body: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.__init__ starts its own background commit thread polling the shared factory-level OffsetTracker. On rebalance the old strategy's thread is never stopped by ResultsStrategyFactory.shutdown and terminate() does not join it, so multiple threads poll the same tracker and invoke different captured commit callables, including revoked-partition commits, causing duplicate commits, commits via invalid closures, and thread leaks.

findings.title: Offsets committed from background thread
findings.body: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy._commit_loop invokes the Arroyo commit callable from a dedicated daemon thread every second instead of from poll/join. Arroyo Commit is expected to be called from the processing thread and is not safe to call concurrently with rebalance/shutdown, risking commits for revoked partitions, races with StreamProcessor shutdown, and lost or mis-ordered commits. Commits should happen synchronously in poll/join.

findings.title: Shutdown abandons queued work instead of draining
findings.body: FixedQueuePool.shutdown sets every worker.shutdown=True before shutting down queues, and OrderedQueueWorker.run loops on while not self.shutdown. Workers therefore exit immediately even when queues still contain submitted WorkItems. SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close() thus discards pending work, leaving offsets never completed to be redelivered in bulk or, if already partially committed, losing ordering guarantees. Shutdown should let workers drain via queue shutdown without a separate flag.

findings.title: decode_payload asserts on FilteredPayload instead of skipping
findings.body: ResultsStrategyFactory.decode_payload asserts not isinstance(payload, FilteredPayload), but SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit passes message.payload which can be FilteredPayload. Every filtered message then raises AssertionError, logs Error submitting message to queue, and only gets skipped via the generic exception path. Filtered payloads are normal and should return None without an exception.

findings.title: wait_until_empty and stats miss in-flight work
findings.body: get_stats and wait_until_empty use Queue.qsize(), which counts only items waiting in the queue, not the item a worker already removed via get() and is still processing. wait_until_empty can return True while workers are still handling results, and total_queued metrics undercount load. Callers using it to decide completion or shutdown can proceed prematurely. Track outstanding work via OffsetTracker outstanding counts or task_done/unfinished_tasks instead of qsize.
